standard_prerequisites.name: Differential graded category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A category enriched in graded modules with a differential on each hom complex satisfying the Leibniz rule with respect to composition.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the ambient setting and supplies the Leibniz rule used throughout the eight identities (source lines 3709-3710, 3740-3741).

standard_prerequisites.name: Admissible short exact sequence in a dg category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A composable pair x -> y -> z for which there is a diagram splitting y as x direct sum z in the graded sense, with the accompanying structure maps.
standard_prerequisites.use: The diagram with the maps a, pi, b, s and the splitting y isomorphic to x direct sum z is the starting point of the proof (source lines 3721-3730).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy of morphisms of complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two morphisms of complexes are homotopic when their difference is of the form d(h) for some graded map h, and homotopic morphisms are equal in the homotopy category.
standard_prerequisites.use: The final two claims are exactly that a delta and delta b are homotopic to zero, which is what makes the compositions vanish in K(A) (source lines 3745-3755).

core_obligations: Extract the splitting: choose the diagram giving the isomorphism y is isomorphic to x direct sum z as graded objects, and record the identities 1 = pi a, 1 = b s, 1 = a pi + s b and pi s = 0 together with their differential consequences (source lines 3721-3740).

Produce the connecting morphism: using the identities d(s) = a pi d(s) and d(pi) = d(pi) s b, show that delta = pi d(s) = -d(pi) s is a morphism of complexes z -> x[1], which needs the computation that d(pi d(s)) = 0 and d(d(pi) s) = 0 (source lines 3740-3749).

Verify that the two compositions vanish in the homotopy category: show a delta = d(s) is homotopic to zero and delta b = d(-pi) is homotopic to zero, which gives the required vanishing of any two consecutive compositions (source lines 3744-3755).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose the splitting diagram for x -> y -> z and note y is isomorphic to x direct sum z as graded objects.
Derive the eight identities among a, pi, b, s and their differentials from the splitting identities and the Leibniz rule.
Use identities (5), (6), (7), (8) to show delta = pi d(s) = -d(pi) s is a morphism of complexes.
Show a delta and delta b are homotopic to zero, giving the vanishing of the consecutive compositions in the homotopy category.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-get-triangle at source lines 3707-3717: for a differential graded category satisfying axioms (A) and (B), an admissible short exact sequence x -> y -> z in the dg category yields a triangle x -> y -> z -> x[1] in the category of complexes such that any two consecutive compositions in z[-1] -> x -> y -> z -> x[1] are zero in the homotopy category. The proof at source lines 3719-3755 has to build the connecting morphism by hand. It starts from a diagram exhibiting the graded splitting y isomorphic to x direct sum z, derives eight identities among the structure maps and their differentials, uses the third identity together with the vanishing of differentials of the split inclusions and projections to show that delta = pi d(s) = -d(pi) s is a morphism of complexes, and finally checks twice that the compositions a delta and delta b are homotopic to zero. The eight identities are not consequences of a stated lemma in this unit; each is obtained by applying the Leibniz rule to one of the splitting identities, and several of them are needed in later steps (identity (7) in the construction of delta, identities (5) and (6) in the vanishing of the two compositions). No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
